name: What problems happen when pool fill-in is done poorly?

mainEntity.name: What are the most common problems after a poorly done pool fill-in?
mainEntity.text: What are the most common problems after a poorly done pool fill-in?

acceptedAnswer.text: Poor pool fill-in work often shows up later as settlement, pooling water, or cracking in whatever was built above it. If the contractor does not punch drainage openings, remove the right parts of the shell, compact in lifts, or test the fill, the area can shift over time. That can create low spots in a lawn, uneven pavers, or drainage problems that send water toward the house. In some cases, the city may fail the final inspection if documentation is incomplete or compaction is not verified. Homeowners should watch for warning signs such as vague scopes, no mention of compaction, no inspection plan, and no explanation of what happens below grade. Good pool fill-in work should be documented, staged, and verified, especially in areas where future landscaping or hardscape is planned.
acceptedAnswer.description: The most common problems are settling, poor drainage, soft spots, uneven grading, cracking in new hardscape, and failed inspections. These issues usually happen when the fill is not compacted properly, drainage holes are missing, or the contractor skips inspection steps. Poor workmanship can create expensive fixes later.
